title: HLabs: plu-ts - ts framework for Cardano smart contracts

ms.promise:
plu-ts ^0.6.*

respective tweet announcing it (present here already)
ms.criteria:
the issue involved incorrect hoisting of "letted" terms in complex contracts.
This issue was identified and solved with plu-ts v0.6.0; introducing a new compilation process, fixing the way letted terms where hashed.
Acceptance criteria can be hence formalized as "fixing letted terms compilation".
the output of the milestone should be considered accepted once letted terms are hoisted as expected

ms.promise:
plu-ts 0.6.5
versions of plu-ts before 0.6.5 where unreliable for the calculation of fees due to plutus costs, this was mainly due to
a bug in the interpretation of the protocol parameters, which was using the memory multiplier of the protocol params for the steps and vice versa, resulting in irrational fees.
ms.criteria:
changes to the plu-ts-offchain package as described in the "outputs " section (that resulted in plu-ts 0.6.5) fixing the bug.
plu-ts 0.6.5 or greather and relative tests should be enough as proof of achievement
the changes in the code can are present in the protocol parameters interpretation, for the same protocol parameters, using the txBuilder before 0.6 and after 0.6.5 will result in more accurate fees, these changes will not yet affect fees due to plutus scripts depending on inputs ordering that will instead be handled in the following milestone(plu-ts 0.7 or higher),

ms.promise:
plu-ts ^0.7.*
the final touch to fix plutus evaluation cost calculation was a bug in the creation of the script context, due to the poorly documented behaviour of the ledger in that regard.
ms.criteria: transactions including plutus scripts that do depend on the inputs ordering in the script context built with plu-ts 0.7 or greater will have accurate fees (and hence not fail due to budget over-spent on submission).

ms.promise:
The proposal mentioned plu-ts v0.8 as final target for this milestone.
however due to the need to integrate plutus V3 and conway ledger definitions in the library, plu-ts' version 0.8 will be used for that purpose, not included in this proposal.
what was originally intended for 0.8 will instead be implemented in version 0.9 and greater.
so plu-ts v0.9 should be considered the output of this milestone.
necessary benchmarks in the two versions will also be output of this milestone, also to fulfill the evidence of completion
ms.criteria:
introduction of enums for better developer experience dealing with types that don't require additional fields informations but need to represent different alternatives (naive example, booleans, currently represented as data constr, can be more efficiently represented via enums)
improvements in standard methods such as `pfind` or anything else depending on the use of `data` conversion, possibly leveraging plutus V3 SoP or alternative representations of structured data (such as `Maybe` as single element list) for plutus v1 and v2.
ms.report:
In this milestone, the focus was on optimizing on-chain contracts compilation
Here I made a video to facilitate the verification of the milestone.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nLNhbRLAhZc
the commit introducing the various optimizations were many, however the last shown in the video is: ce34ff8e0ce5cdc833dfec4f254fba271e657d85
all commits are publicly available at: https://github.com/HarmonicLabs/plu-ts/network
additionally, as specified in the milestone outputs, here is the benchmarks repo, showing the effects of the optimizations implemented: https://github.com/HarmonicLabs/plu-ts-bench
Enums where ultimately not implemented because it didn't improve contracts performances as originally expected.
The tweet highlighting performance improvements can be found here: https://x.com/MicheleHarmonic/status/1860478467864723860
